Thanks for the loop. I had a quick scan of the attached MSA and flagged a couple of priority items that will affect redline scope:

1) SLA language — they reference a 90-day review window; need to confirm whether this is a proposed obligation or a request to revisit terms after 90 days. If it's an obligation language, we will need to map to our latency/availability SLOs and propose a fallback.

2) Data residency clause — Onyx has a us-west residency note; confirm whether all processing is expected in that region or just storage. If it's processing, we'll need to check capacity with infra (David please confirm GPU pool availability in us-west for reserved lanes).

3) Exhibit A party sheet — several parties listed without signer/role clarity. Marissa, can you own a canonical party matrix and return a version with: primary signer, backup signer, billing contact, security contact, and KMS owner if applicable?

For redline cadence, we can return a marked-up Word with our preferred edits and an alternate clean copy with a comment slate for bigger negotiation points. If Onyx prefers a single doc, say so and we'll prioritize.

I will aim to provide a first-pass redline (comments first, clean redline as time permits) by EOD Monday PST. If anything here is time-sensitive (procurement deadlines, go/no-go dates), share those so we can prioritize.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracting | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
